author: hattrill
body:
The human, rat and mouse NGRN Neugrin genes/proteins are annotated with nuclear and secreted GO terms from various sources.
UniProtKB:Q9NPE2 
MGI:1933212
RGD:1583734

I've looked at it and it appears to be a mitochondrial protein localized to the matrix that acts at 16s mt rRNA processing/at or prior to large mitoribosome assembly.

Both claude.pro and jupyter gene-review agree on this:

There is no real biological controversy. NGRN is a mitochondrial matrix protein. The nuclear and secreted annotations are legacy artefacts from the original 2000 cloning paper that have propagated through the databases and never been retracted.

Adding the claude summary doc to the ticket. 

[NGRN_localization.docx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33150667/NGRN_localization.docx)
